probing_questions: Name each answerable subquestion and its evidential test; include contemporary examples, historical analogies, conceptual treatment and potential contrary evidence as the question requires.

Produce 12–32 distinct literal words or phrases for case-insensitive substring search: variants, near-synonyms, named episodes and historical vocabulary justified by this question and supplied context. No Boolean syntax or invented event names. Search unexpected conceptual formulations, not only words in the question.

engine_name: Plan a question across an author's work
problematique: Investigate the supplied question about the named author, building on existing profiles, citation ledgers, prior readings, secondary analyses and Referee context. Separate the publication date from the historical period discussed. Treat the stated event in the question as a question, never as an established fact. Profiles, search matches, prior memos, citations and Referee descriptions are leads, not the author's testimony. Attribute interlocutors, interviewers, coauthors and quoted opponents carefully. Only supplied primary text supports direct claims about what the author says. Citation co-occurrence is a retrieval route, not proof of substantive engagement. Search absence, unread material and missing text never establish that the author never discusses a topic. State the actual corpus and window coverage. Keep uncertainty, counterevidence and unresolved cases. Use literal independent source anchors, preserving negation and qualifications. Never invent a quote, page or source id. An edition, reprint, translated edition or container publication date does not establish a new intervention; consult supplied date/edition metadata and flag unresolved original dates. A book-section container is not the author's own chapter unless the packet establishes authorship. Quotes marked quote_verified false are conjectures and cannot support a direct answer.
